utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we hear the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to go on record in public about a couple of matters that occurred yesterday, because I think the record needs to be clear and I think that perhaps some sanctions need to be considered. The Prosecutor yesterday, Mr. McCloskey himself, stood up and said - and I'm reading from the transcript, this is in regards to new evidence that they have that he talks about - "one example is I believe you acquitted on is the issue of the people who were in the interrogation notes that were found with Resid Sinanovic. We now have, courtesy of the Defence, seen the lawyer, those notes and has actually interviewed those people in front of the brigade command, and they are also on the missing list." I want to point out that Mr. Zlatan Celanovic was interviewed by the Prosecution on 4 December 2003. He provided some notes. He was then interviewed on December 10, 2003. The Prosecution closed its case on 27 February 2004. They had all that information. They chose not to put it in their case because, I dare say, they had concluded that it had no real value as to that particular issue. And now it would appear - and this is the second time that a remark such as this was made, and I will get to the reasons as to the motivations behind the remark - but it would appear that Mr. McCloskey was being utterly dishonest with this Trial Chamber. And I'm using -- I'm choosing my words very carefully. Normally I would call him something other than that, much stronger, much more closer to the bone, and closer to what actually he is doing. Secondly, yesterday he indicated that now we know that some 50 bodies in each classroom at the Vuk Karadzic have been discovered, courtesy of the Defence of course. And if we look at the record, first of all, there is no such thing, there is no such testimony that 50 bodies in each classroom at the Vuk Karadzic school were found. Second of all, the individual that was brought here by the Defence to present that testimony, aside from the fact that he was never a member of the Bratunac Brigade, but that individual who testified in open court, Dragan Mirkovic, was initially interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution on 13 October 2000. He testified on 21st April 2004. Of course that was well in advance of the Prosecution to file for an appeal to the judgement of acquittal, which it now seeks to reverse or put in abeyance something that is not called for in the rules, nor does it can exist in the Anglo-Saxon system once a judgement is entered. Now, I'm mentioning this because I think these sorts of dishonest statements do not belong in this Tribunal. Secondly, when we look at the comments by Mr. McCloskey, it appears they are designed for another purpose, and the purpose is to interfere with the attorney/client relationship. Albeit that relationship is strained, I think that's what is designed to suggest that the Defence is now putting on evidence that is harmful to the client is solely designed for that purpose. I frankly do not mind and indeed welcome vigorous advocacy. I think that's what an adversarial procedure should be. I don't appreciate dishonesty in the Court, especially when it comes from an officer of the Court; and I think the United Nations deserves something better than that. So I want the record to be clear, first of all they had that information. Nothing was disclosed by the Defence that they didn't have. They made some tactical decisions. Secondly, the record as they stated it to be is false, and that was an intentional falsehood. And I suggest, Your Honour, that perhaps some cautionary instructions should be issued to the Prosecutor. If he wishes to take personal shots at me, I don't care. After 20 years, I've developed a rather thick skin. But I do take offence to when somebody is manipulating the facts and being dishonest with the Trial Chamber for the sole purpose of trying to salvage a case, particularly as we have seen in this one, where the Prosecution in essence, in my humble opinion has turned incompetence into an art form when it has come to investigating their case, and even presenting their case. That's all I have on this matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I think it's a very serious allegation you put on the record. And we should hear the other side on this very issue. And everybody will have an opportunity to present their view. Yes. I see Mr. McCloskey is standing. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That perhaps is the single most outrageous comment I have ever heard a lawyer utter in court. And I will refrain from going through his history or anything else related towards him. But I will talk to you of some of the substance of what he said. Yes, Mr. Celanovic was interviewed by us and, yes, we had that information. There's no doubt about that; that's not hidden. However, we chose to get that information related to those other witnesses, those other Muslims, that were interviewed in the same notes as Resid Sinanovic, we chose to bring that information in through Mr. Butler and Mr. Butler's report where he talks about all of those notes being found at the security office and that all of the people on those notes to be on the missing list. And we used the evidence related to Resid Sinanovic that we had from (redacted) - I think (redacted), and Momir Nikolic to be the representative sample of those people. And as such we didn't feel it necessary to bring in Mr. Celanovic, who, as you saw it, was an extremely adverse hostile witness to the Prosecution, to prove something we'd felt we had already proven. Now, as it turns out when we offered those notes into evidence, the Court did not accept them because Mr. Butler didn't speak directly to them, so the Court decided to set them aside in their 98 bis ruling, all perfectly understandable. My understanding was those things were set aside by the Court in an understandable situation where we didn't get all the evidence we chose to get in. Then Mr. Karnavas called Mr. Celanovic up there, so all that material became again authenticated specifically by the person that did the interviews, so all that material comes in. That is just one example of several key pits of evidence that has been provided by the Defence case in our case. And this happens in most cases. This is not some personal attack on Mr. Karnavas. The Bosanski Samac case, they put on 99 witnesses. If you look at the judgement, you'll, I think, see the Court naturally found Prosecution evidence in some of those 99 witnesses; it's inevitable. This is what I was talking about. And we will see many, many more examples. It's frankly shocking to me that the extent of the evidence that's coming on through the Defence case. The first example we saw was when Mr. Karnavas provided Mile Petrovic to back up Momir Nikolic's story of travelling along the road, calling down witness -- calling down Muslims. That was an uncorroborated Momir Nikolic story until Mile Petrovic showed up on the scene. So this is something that is part of his strategy and it's -- it's a fine strategy from his perspective, I'm sure. But we see witness after witness that helps provide us -- provide evidence for us, and that's all I was pointing out. Because we're getting more evidence, and then of course Witness 130 is added to that. Now, the witness regarding the 50 bodies is -- well, I think it was a protected witness, but it was -- if you recall, it was 50 -- he received reports of 50 bodies, and he stated that there was body -- he had heard reports that there was bodies in every classroom on each floor of that building, not 50 bodies in each classroom. I don't think I said that, and if I did, that was a mistake. So these two examples of this incredible allegation amount to nothing. And I understand there's a sensitivity in the client situation here, and I have tried to stay away from that as much as I could. And I have instructed my people to ignore the constant personal attacks on each of them, which if you may remember began with Stacey de la Torre and her wonderful response that was not going to respond to these childish barbs. Well, I don't think I need to respond any further. I think this Court knows what's going on here, and I think -- I hope the Court will keep in mind the ethical rules of this Tribunal. And I know they do. And I meant to memorise the ethical code that speaks of dealing with each other and each colleagues, and I don't remember it right now. But as I say, this is something that I have never seen in my life; I hope to never see it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I stand by my comments, Your Honour. I just stand by my comments and my interpretation of what he said yesterday with respect to this new-founded evidence. They had all of this evidence, and now we're hearing a different tune being sung to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I believe that in this trial we spend much more time on the relationship between the parties. It seems to me there is a tense relationship. And sometimes it comes to the personal attacks which this Court would not like to see. The time and the resources allocated to this case are very limited, so have to make the best use of it and spend much more time hearing the witness rather than the parties. So I hope that in the future the parties could talk to each other out of court first. If there are some differences - of course there should be some differences between the parties - that could not be solved and it's very serious, you could bring to the attention of this Bench and we'll see what we shall do. Now we are in the middle of these proceedings; it's very difficult at this stage for us to make any rulings in this direction. I hope that at the end of this trial we'll see a more clear picture on all the things the parties raised today. This is all I could say at this moment. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's one other matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- with respect to not this witness but the following witness. If we could go to closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I will need you to speak up just a little bit. You don't have to lean forward, but you need to raise your voice just a little bit. Could you please tell us your name, sir.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Borivoje Jakovljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: J-a-k-o-v-l-j-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what you do today for a living.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I own a minifarm, a small farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in 1995, in July, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what your position was with the Bratunac Brigade, or within the Bratunac Brigade I should say.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was a soldier in the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long you had been with the Bratunac Brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: From the spring of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before becoming a military police officer with the Bratunac Brigade, did you have any background or training in being a military police, policeman I should say?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you do your JNA training when you were younger?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were in the JNA, could you please tell us what training you received.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was trained for work in the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So while you were trained -- when you said no, earlier, I take it that was with relation to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you completed your military service, were you in the reserves as part of the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the reserve force of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And prior to the commencement of the war, that is, from the time that you left your JNA service until 1992, could you please tell us what you were doing for a living.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was employed in a local firm, working on the maintenance of electrical machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you mobilised in 1992 in the Territorial Defence, the TO, when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was first mobilised to the reserve force of the civilian police. And later I left them and joined the detachment that it was first known as, and later the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you joined the Bratunac Brigade, in what capacity or what function did you carry out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was a private.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which company or battalion?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion, an infantry battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention from now on to the events surrounding the -- Srebrenica, the events concerning Srebrenica. That would be in July 1995 and thereafter. And I'm going to give you two dates for points of reference, one being July 6th, which is a fixed date that we know when the events commenced towards Srebrenica, and then July 11th, the date when Srebrenica actually fell. So first of all, could you please tell us whether you had received any special instructions or special orders prior to July 6th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, at about that time, what were your normal duties, what were you carrying out, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The most frequent activities we engaged in at that time were to secure roads between Bratunac, Sase, and Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other duties did you have in addition to those, or functions I should say?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Normal, ordinary duties and functions, to sanction disciplinary offences when soldiers left their positions on the front, and things like that. And to bring them back to their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have heard testimony in this court that on occasion military police could be used for combat. Do you recall whether during the events concerning Srebrenica, that would be from July 6th and onwards, whether you or other members of the Bratunac Brigade military police were engaged in any military activities?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: During that month, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did anything unusual happen from July 6th to July 11th, that period that I've indicated, the commencement to the fall of Srebrenica? Anything unusual that you recall.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall where you were on July 11th, 1995, that is the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was on the road, Bratunac/Sase/Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you been at that road?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm unable to tell you exactly, but we returned in the afternoon. Now, what time it was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you returned, could you please tell us where you went. And I take it you returned back to Bratunac, that's what you're referring?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where you went first.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: To the headquarters of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you received any orders upon your arrival there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So could you please tell us what you did the rest of the afternoon or evening on the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the evening we were deployed to Bratunac, the Fontana Hotel, to provide security of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who it was that deployed you -- that issued the order for you and, I would gather from your answer, other military police who were ordered to go to Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was customary for orders to be passed on to the soldier on duty. Now, in this particular case I can't remember who was the soldier on duty. So that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you saw Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know who Momir Nikolic is, though?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us about what time it was when you went to Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when you arrived there what instructions, if any, you received and from whom.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember from whom I received instructions. There were several of us. The outside security of the hotel, nothing more than that, more specific than that. We were told to secure the hotel on the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what exactly you did and for how long.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything in particular. As far as I can remember it was the normal physical security of the hotel that we were providing and of the People's University, as it is right next to the hotel. Now, I am not quite sure whether it was that same evening or the next day that I spent some time with members of the Dutch Battalion in the secondary school centre. Now, whether that was that same evening or the following evening, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were the Dutch Battalion or members of the Dutch Battalion doing in the secondary school in the centre of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They were accommodated there. There's an amphitheatre there. They were sittings, sleeping, resting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall about -- first of all, were there any incidents that night that you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't recall any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time you completed your duty there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was there all night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the morning came, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I went to have breakfast in the restaurant where we regularly had our meals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be where?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the command building next to the command of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having your breakfast, did you receive any other orders?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing special, just to go back to where we had been before, that is, around the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many of you received that order?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time it would have been - and now we're speaking of July 12, 1995 - what time it would have been that you returned to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: After breakfast, I don't know exactly. Anyway, it was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you went there, could you please tell us to whom you reported, if anyone.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Before I arrived to the Fontana Hotel, about 50 metres from the hotel a vehicle, a military vehicle, stopped. And they called me. I recognised General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who called you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Mladic himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what kind of a mood was he in?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He was in a good mood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did he have any instructions for you or did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you like to share that with us?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said: "When the transport starts from Potocari, I don't want to see anyone on the street, no one. Do you understand me?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand what he was talking about when he said, "When the transport starts from Potocari... " Did you understand what he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how is it that you understand -- that you understood what he was speaking about?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There were rumours already, and we saw buses that were ready, buses and trucks. And the story was that people would be coming out of Potocari, that is, the Muslims, the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had anyone said or had you heard as to where these buses and trucks would be heading towards?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No one told me personally anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you please tell us what you did after General Mladic gave you those instructions.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Close to the hotel there is a junction, and I was there all the time because that is where vehicles have to slow down and take a left, turning towards Zvornik. So we spent most of our time there at that crossroads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say "we," how many were there of you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: With me, there was another colleague of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one minor detail. When General Mladic gave you this order, did you by any chance inform General Mladic that you needed to check with your commander, or your komandir, to see whether you could carry out the order that General Mladic was issuing to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I couldn't say that to him then; I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not? He wasn't your commander.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic, I had a lot of respect for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you contact Mirko Jankovic, your komandir; or Momir Nikolic, the head of security and intelligence; or Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, to inform them, any of them, what you were carrying out, what orders you were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long were you at that juncture?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how long, but throughout the day while the transport was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see who was in the buses and trucks? Were you paying attention?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what you noticed.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that there were mostly women and children and elderly, and they were few, few elderly men. Later on, I didn't pay any more attention because I was busy dealing with our own local civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Curiosity of our locals. We had to move them away from the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you notice any incidents, anyone reacting toward the buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't have a chance because we kept them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that they were -- once they would make that turn, they would head in the direction towards Zvornik. Did you notice whether any of those buses or trucks at any point in time during the day made any turns into the city centre?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after the -- at what point do you recall was it when you left that location?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Back to the command, to have dinner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did anyone give you permission or did you seek permission from anyone to leave your post to go to the brigade command in order to have dinner?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Because I saw that the transport was completed, I stayed on for a while and then I returned. And it was getting dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having dinner, do you recall whether you received any other orders for that evening? And now we're speaking of the evening of July 12th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular. I was informed that we were going back to the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go back to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what the lighting conditions were when you arrived back at the Hotel Fontana, so at least we can have some sort of an opinion as to what time --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was evening already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please tell us whether you reported to anyone once you arrived at Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing specific. I found my colleagues there. We made a timetable. I don't remember if there were any commanders around. We made a timetable as to who would be inside, who would be outside from what time to what time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this night, the night of July 12th, 1995, did you spend the entire night outside, as you had the previous night?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how you spent the night and where.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I spent half that night outside, and from midnight onwards I was in the hallway where the rooms are. General Mladic slept in one of those rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he was in one of those rooms?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The shift before me told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did General Mladic get out -- go out of his room during the night while you were there guarding the hallway?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, not until the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic in the morning?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now we're speaking about the morning of July 13, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about what time it would have been when you saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him or did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He addressed us first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us what exactly he said.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He greeted us and asked us to find him a shaving kit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have anymore words with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, do you recall what you did the morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The usual. I went to have breakfast and went back to the road to my place near the junction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The same place where you had been the previous day, July 12?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether someone had ordered you to return or whether this was on your own initiative.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody ordered me to do so. I suppose my superiors knew about the duties given me by Mladic, and nobody asked me anything. I just did the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us how long you were there that day.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly, maybe until the afternoon. I don't know until what time. It was past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was, but it was already afternoon. General Mladic came by again, accompanied by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And -- well, how was he -- in what sort of vehicle did he come by?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: A vehicle that we referred to as P-U-H, PUH. It was a military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you colleagues located?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Another military vehicle called Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how many colleagues were there with the general.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I could not tell you that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall who the other -- who the colleagues were? Do you recall any of them, their names? I know it's been almost 10 years.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The driver was Milovan Mitrovic. I remember another one of our colleagues, Slobodan Mijatovic. And I also remember another man, Bosko, whose last name I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the general stop or did you just notice him driving by?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We stood there for some time -- I don't remember. I got orders to get into the vehicle together with them. I don't remember who conveyed that order to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't whether it was Mladic or one of your colleagues or someone else?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't Mladic; it was one of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you get into the Pinzgauer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us where you went from there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: A bit later we moved on, first General Mladic's vehicle then our vehicle, towards Kravica, Kravica village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, the Pinzgauer was behind the vehicle that General Mladic was in?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you got to Kravica did the -- do you recall whether there were any stops in that location, at or near Kravica?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Not in Kravica, the first village after Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what the name of that village is?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us what you saw when you stopped at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we saw soldiers. The soldiers were standing in the street and around, and the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us first of all, the soldiers, did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know them. They were not troops from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: By their uniforms. And then I didn't recognise any of the commanding officers, in fact, I didn't recognise the commanding officer who addressed Mladic at that point; whereas, I knew all the commanding officers of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get to what you saw with respect to General Mladic, could you please tell us approximately how many Muslim prisoners you noticed.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I would not like to guess, and I cannot tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where they were located.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the street in a meadow. They were sitting in that meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said "the right-hand side of the street," in which direction are we talking, heading -- going towards Konjevic Polje or going towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you get out of the vehicle when General Mladic got out of his?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point at that location did you get out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall approximately how far you were from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: About 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you paying attention as to what was going on, or were you lost in your thoughts?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear what General Mladic discussed with the officer in charge of those troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: But I did hear when General Mladic addressed the prisoners, he was speaking in a loud voice. And I understood the main drift of what he was saying. I don't remember it word for word, but I remember the essence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, and I want to go step by step, when the cars, the vehicles I should say, stopped in Sandici, who -- General Mladic got out of his vehicle, as I understand you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please tell us what exactly he did once he got out of his vehicle. What did he do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: First he was looking for the commander in charge of those troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he find the person?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: That officer came up to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long did General Mladic speak with this officer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're referring to this individual as an officer. Do you know whether he had a rank, or this an assumption on your part that since he was a komandir, a commanding officer, that it would logically follow that he was, in fact, an officer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I saw by his insignia that he was an officer. I just didn't know the rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. After General Mladic briefly spoke with this individual, could you please tell us what did General Mladic do next, if anything.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, he approached the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us: How close was General Mladic to the prisoners when he was speaking to this officer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He was maybe 20 metres away from them, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was General Mladic from the prisoners when he was addressing the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He was right by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a mood was General Mladic in?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In my judgement, a good mood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he address these prisoners, in what tone of voice, in what manner?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: First he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he insult them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he yelling at these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. He informed them that they -- their families were taken care of and that there were no problems. He asked them to be patient because it was a very hot day. He asked them to be patient, that everything would be fine. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall for how long General Mladic addressed this group of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He talked with them for a while, and at the end he asked if anybody had any special needs. It could have been 20 minutes; I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When General Mladic inquired whether any of them had any special needs, did any of the prisoners speak up?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you were able to hear what, if any, special needs were being noted by these prisoners to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't hear the prisoners speaking, because they spoke in a not-so-loud voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during this period did you notice whether any other Muslim males were coming and surrendering themselves?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many there were?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything specific. A group came up carrying a seriously wounded soldier of theirs. I noticed one or two maybe who were less seriously wounded in the same group, because they were passing by the vehicle in which I was and laid him down. They laid him down, this wounded person. There was nothing going on, no shooting, nothing that I could hear. So I asked them what had happened and they said when they had been up there in the forest they had two options. One option was to surrender, and there was a group among them who was in favour of that; and another group was against it. And they clashed amongst themselves. And some shooting started even. That's how it happened, and they were looking for a doctor. There was no doctor around. One of my colleagues gave them a first aid kit, bandages, and they bandaged him, but that was not enough. So I gave them mine, because that person was very seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said earlier that when you were there you did not hear any shooting going on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear any artillery, shelling, from further distances?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. There was nothing that you could hear. Everything was quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Approximately how long were you there with General Mladic in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. Maybe 30, 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one last question before we move on. When you heard General Mladic speaking to the Muslim prisoners, telling them that they didn't need to worry about anything, that they would be joining their families, did you believe General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Why wouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to that had you heard, either from General Mladic or anyone else, that there had been some plan put in motion to execute any Muslim that the Serb army could get their hands on?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no discussion about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after Sandici, could you please tell us where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the same direction, towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the next stop was.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We stopped very briefly at the junction in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose for that stop, do you know?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There was a checkpoint held by the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice there at that juncture whether there were any military police of the Bratunac Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade, that is, individuals that you would recognise by face and perhaps even by uniform to be soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see anyone from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain at Konjevic Polje, at this juncture?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's sort of relative. Minute-wise, could you tell us what do you mean by "very briefly"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly. Mladic had a sudden change of mood. He cursed those civilian policemen there, scolded them. I don't know for what reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, first of all do you recall whether General Mladic got out of his vehicle this time, as he had done previously in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you noticed any prisoners there, Muslim prisoners, at that point in time when you were at that intersection with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier I asked you if you knew Momir Nikolic, as I understand also goes by the nickname Penzijica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know him fairly well?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it by that point in time had you seen him someplace, you know, in the middle of the road standing there, dressed in his uniform with his Ray Ban sunglasses, as was his style, you would have been able to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I would have been able to recognise, had I seen him, but I don't remember having seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what my question is. Because we've heard testimony from Momir Nikolic, no less under oath, where he stated - and this can be found on the record, for those who may wish to know, on page 1718, that is 1.718 here when his testimony was taken on Monday, 22nd September 2003 - but he stated at that point in time, General Mladic was out of the vehicle, he approached General Mladic to give some sort of a report, that he was able to notice some prisoners, and that upon asking General Mladic what the fate of the prisoners would be, General Mladic made the hand gesture like this. And in fact, we can see that on the video, on the video transcript of his testimony. Sir, did you see Momir Nikolic approach General Mladic for a -- what we could call a tete-a-tete for Momir Nikolic to give a report to General Mladic at Konjevic Polje on 13 July 1995, as he would have us believe?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing Momir Nikolic there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just for the record, and just so that we are precise, before coming here today, sir, last night did I not show you in your language the video clip, the video testimony, of Momir Nikolic concerning this particular segment of his testimony under oath? Do you recall seeing that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall his vivid description of the events as he recalled them while under oath testifying on direct examination, being questioned by the Prosecutor? Do you recall his description?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have an opinion as to whether Momir Nikolic, in light of what you were able to see at the time and given the fact that you were with General Mladic at the time, do you have an opinion as to whether was testifying truthfully or untruthfully in this court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that question. The witness can't comment on the veracity of another witness. That's totally inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please rephrase this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic's description accurate, that is, consistent with reality, consistent with the facts as you know them to be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness testified that he couldn't remember whether Momir Nikolic was there, so I don't see how he could ask that follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you -- was Momir Nikolic there? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the testimony that you saw, the video clip that you saw, in your opinion was that accurate or inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it was inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now -- and just one final point. I want to make sure. Did General Mladic get out of his vehicle in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that he got out of his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remember that he was scolding or yelling at the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through the window of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe this may be a good time to break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I believe we left off when you were in Konjevic Polje with General Mladic on July 13th, 1995. Could you please tell us: From there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We set off towards Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you make any stops?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us where.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: At a location before Milici called Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please just tell us what the distance is from Konjevic Polje to Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but under 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened, if anything, when you stopped at Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The same scene was repeated as we had at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to go step by step here again. Could you please tell us first of all whether General Mladic got out of his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you got out of the Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall -- you said it was the same as Sandici, so can I conclude that there were prisoners there as well?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us approximately how many prisoners there were.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'd rather not make any estimates because I'm absolutely not sure. I can't even approximate the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it look like a large group? More than 10 -- or a small group, 10 or 20?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Somewhat more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall where they were exactly, the location?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They were sitting on the grass in the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you drive towards Milici and you go by Kasaba, are you able to see the football stadium from the road itself?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us whether anyone was guarding the Muslim prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us who they were, if you know.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers I did not know. I didn't recognise anyone -- any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were able to tell us that at Sandici you were able to notice that the soldiers there were not from the Bratunac Brigade, their uniforms, and also you indicated that they had some sort of insignia. Do you recall whether the soldiers at Kasaba had the same sort of uniforms and the same insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember about the insignia, but the uniforms were similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question about this. Do you know whether they were soldiers, military police, or special police, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There were some special police, but not military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How did you know that there were some military police there -- I mean, some special police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They had blue uniforms on them, some sort of combination of blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any officers there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice who they were -- well, let me rephrase. Did you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the komandir, the commanding officer, of the unit of those soldiers that were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the special police was from, which unit?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any dogs there, the police dogs I'm referring to, German shepherd-type?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long you were at this location.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Again, 30 or 40 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that have been about the same amount of time as you and the others, along with General Mladic, had spent in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us how close you were to General Mladic when you exited the Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were close, maybe 5 metres between us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was there a particular purpose for getting out of the Pinzgauer and coming within a 5-metre radius of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No special reason. Only in this case the stadium was further away from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please describe to us what exactly General Mladic did.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He did the same as he did at Sandici, he called on the officer in command, he exchanged just a few words with him hastily, and then he approached the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, first of all were you able to hear this time, since you were out of the Pinzgauer and closer to General Mladic, were you able to hear what the exchange was between General Mladic and the officer of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything. They just exchanged a couple of words very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were the prisoners at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Mladic walked in amongst them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do when Mladic walked amongst them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were standing there. This was on the edge of the pitch. Mladic went in deeper, and we were standing behind his back outside the pitch, on the edge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did Mladic have his special protection unit, his own security that he normally travelled with?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: While he was with us, he only had one man who was next to him nonstop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from where Mladic was standing, were you able to hear what he was saying this time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us what you heard.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: First of all he greeted them. He asked them: "Do you know who I am?" Later he introduced himself. And in principle, he repeated what he had said at Sandici. He stayed a little longer -- actually, he devoted a little more time on the question of whether anyone had anything in particular to say. As there were quite a number of those who had some special requests, he called on the officer and he told him -- I don't remember how he addressed him, what rank he used, but he said: "Look into this and deal with it together with the people in question."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did General Mladic's mood change from the previous time when he had stopped in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. He used the same tone of voice and he spoke in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was he abusive in any way toward the prisoners in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't insult them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, were you able to hear any military activity, ongoing military activities, such as shooting or shelling?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember hearing anything. It was quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you noticed anyone surrendering while you were in Kasaba, as you had seen, for instance, in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. People were approaching quite freely. They were searched at the entrance to the playground, and then they sat down. But there were fewer than there were at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know where they were coming from, these folks that were surrendering themselves?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As the pitch is on the right-hand side of the road, I noticed one or two coming from the woods on the left-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they being escorted or were they coming on their own, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: On their own. They didn't have anyone escorting them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from Kasaba where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Vlasenica from Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps some 20-odd kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us where exactly you went in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in front of the building of the main headquarters of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived there, could you please tell us what, if anything, did you do.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We got out of the vehicle to rest for a while, and we were invited to dinner because it was evening already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you given any orders while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time this would have been?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Early evening, the evening. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long you were in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We spent a little more time there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's rather relative. We know that you spent by your estimation 30 to 40 minutes in Sandici and at Kasaba. Would that have been about the same amount of time or more?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: A bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where exactly were you invited to eat?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the restaurant there, inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were eating at the restaurant, did you notice whether there were any other officers, VRS officers, be they from the Main Staff, the Drina Corps, the Bratunac Brigade, or any other brigade for that matter?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice anyone from the Bratunac Brigade. I noticed officers, but I don't know where they were serving. They were hurrying to go to a meeting. It was my understanding that they were going to a conference room; that was what they talked about amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did -- was General Mladic in the restaurant while you were there eating?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that point in time General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I did see General Krstic on the 11th and 12th, but only in passing, only then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in Vlasenica, in the restaurant, while you were there resting and eating?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you invited while you were in Vlasenica to attend any meetings that might have been held?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you go from Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us: Where did you stop on the way towards Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: On the way to Han Pijesak we first stopped -- I don't know the name of the location, but there was a base there for maintenance of roads in wintertime. We stopped there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for stopping there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Mladic probably knew, because he stopped there. When we stopped and entered this compound, we found there some 15 or so civilian policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They were sitting there, resting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was General Mladic's reaction?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very stormy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, describe to us in detail exactly what you were able to see.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Mladic simply went mad. He was very nervous. He cursed. He asked who was the officer in command. He wanted him to report to him. He repeated that a couple of times until the commanding officer of the unit did come up to him. Afterwards, the officer was punished. Mladic's personal escort slapped this commanding officer himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else get slapped?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that, what happened?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He ordered them to pick up their weapons, and wherever they were deployed to go and take up their positions and do their duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how long you were at this location?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did General Mladic calm down after punishing the civilian police commander and sending them off to wherever they were supposed to be located and deployed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He got into the vehicle, but I didn't notice that he had calmed down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Shortly after that we stopped again. We came across two vehicles coming towards us. As far as I can remember, they introduce themselves as being Medicins Sans Frontieres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what happened?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: They ordered them to get out of the vehicle as well. We didn't interfere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they foreigners, or were they Serbian or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you hear what exchange, if any, General Mladic had with them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He yelled at them very briefly, that they were smugglers, good-for-nothings, and the greatest traitors of the Serb people, or words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that, what did General Mladic do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He was very nervous then too. He ordered us to stop vehicles passing by going in the opposite direction, going towards us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it when you say "nervous" in that sense of the word, in your language, you mean angry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- so what was he -- do you know why he was so angry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Because of those policemen down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it just the sight of regular police would set him off?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I noticed as we went along that he didn't like them much, he didn't stand them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after that what did General Mladic do, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We stopped the vehicles. And if there were men, he would order them to go to the front line. If there were no men inside, able-bodied men of military age, there were no problems, they could pass on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, which front line was he sending these people to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, because I don't really know my way around in that area. He simply ordered them to go and take up positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long did you stay there carrying out these activities, that is, stopping cars and with Mladic telling the male drivers to go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And from there what -- after that, what happened?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We got into the vehicles and continued on our way to Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go all the way to Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us where the next stop was.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: At a petrol station just before entering Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the purpose for stopping there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We needed to refuel our tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after refueling your tanks, what happened? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He asked us: "Fellows, we've arrived. Are you going on with me or are you going back?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where he was going to? Did he announce a particular place?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the response?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had indicated earlier that when you got into the Pinzgauer you noticed that there were three other members of the Bratunac Brigade military police. Do you recall who was the komandir amongst you? Was there someone in charge?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think there was anyone in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you were silent. Is there a reason why you were silent? After all, here was General Mladic inviting you to go on.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were very tired. We had been going on without sleep for a long time. But he interrupted us. Quickly he said: "I know, fellows, that you are tired. No problem. You can go back."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he say anything else to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us exactly what you recall, to the best that you can, what General Mladic said.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Something like this, he said: "Go back. No problem. All the rest will be dealt with by Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Beara." Something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. First of all, did you know Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I only saw him once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what General Mladic was referring to when he said words to the effect that: The rest will be dealt with by Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Beara, whatever the rank was that he used?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't give it any thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't you ask him: "General, sir, what do you mean by Beara will deal with the rest?" Weren't you curious?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't dare to speak to Mladic like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
