utterances.text: After the scenes we had witnessed at the entrance to Han Pijesak, we didn't dare ask him any questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, since we're with Colonel Beara, let me ask a few questions. We said that the activities commenced against Srebrenica around July 6th, with Srebrenica falling on July 11th. You told us what you did the evening of July 11th as well as your activities for July 12th and 13th. Could you please tell us, sir, during that stretch of period did you at any point in time see Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us about what time would it have been when General Mladic spoke to you at the gas station as you go towards Han Pijesak, at the outskirts of Han Pijesak? What time would this have been?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was the evening. It was already dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, from there what did you and the other members of the Bratunac Brigade military police do?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We made a U-turn and went in the opposite direction, towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where was your final destination that evening?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about what time did you arrive in Bratunac, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was already late. I couldn't tell you the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether you noticed anything unusual as you were driving from the stretch of road of the intersection of Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that stretch of road, there is as I understand it, it would be on your right side coming from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac, the Kravica agricultural warehouse. Are you aware of that, that structure?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would I be correct in stating that it is relatively near the road itself?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: About 20 metres from the street, from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall when passing that particular structure, that stretch of the road, whether you noticed any unusual activity going on?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anything special. It was the evening, it was dark, night in fact. There was no lighting around, and we passed quickly because the road from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac was unsafe. It was not safe at all and we were driving fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, did you drive fast throughout the entire stretch of your return, that is, from the Han Pijesak area all the way to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Up to Konjevic Polje we did not drive fast. We were not in a hurry. And from Konjevic Polje onwards, we drove much faster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that stretch of road that you drove much faster, were you able to -- did you hear any ongoing shooting?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Occasionally. Single shots, occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any earth-moving equipment, any large construction equipment, with lighting perhaps, that would at least give the impression that there was ongoing activity going on somewhere in that -- on that stretch of the road?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stop at any point on that stretch of the road, Konjevic Polje/Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was driving, incidentally, just to make sure? I think you might have told us already, but who was driving the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Milovan Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did he drive it both on the way towards Han Pijesak and then back towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to Bratunac could you please tell us where you went.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We returned to the military police base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once you returned there, could you please tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived, there was no one around, only the officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any specific orders or instructions upon your arrival?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say "nothing specific," was there something that was nonspecific?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We were told that everybody was in town, because we had asked about the others, and we were told they were in town. They told us to go and get some rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So getting back to my earlier question: Were you given a specific task to carry out that particular evening, that you recall, that is?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that we were given any specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in light of what you had learned from the duty officer, what, if anything, you did next.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there for a short while, and then we left the base and went into town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went into town, were you carrying any weapons?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We always carry our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what weapons were you in particular carrying?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us where you went.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I went into town. It was very close by, 200, 300 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could get you to be a little more specific. Where exactly in town did you go to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There is one street when you get into the high street, there is a street that runs towards the school. It is on the way to my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is -- I take it that street if you're going from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, you come out, you get to the main road, you walk down the main road. Then you would take a left to go to the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same road that one would find the bakery, a small bakery?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the stadium, the football stadium, if one was taking that -- the route that you took, would you be going by the stadium?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be in close proximity of the stadium?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: About a hundred metres away, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want you to think back. I know it's rather difficult to think back close to ten years. But as you were taking that walk from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters on the main road, down, taking that left, and as you were getting within the vicinity of the stadium, did you hear any shooting going on at that time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Everything was quiet at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say "everything was quiet," so I take it, since it's at night, it's rather quiet, had there been shooting going on at that particular time, would you have been able to hear it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever -- before coming here today, have you ever heard of any shooting going on, either in the afternoon, evening, or night in that stadium, which is more or less in the middle of Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that perhaps Momir Nikolic was among the shooters there, carrying out these sorts of atrocious activities?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular night, did you see Momir Nikolic, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us where exactly you went. You said you were walking down, you took that left. Now, where are you going and what are you doing?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I came to the beginning of that street and I saw vehicles parked there, buses, freight trucks. On the freight trucks, I noticed that they had no tarpaulins. I saw people on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who they were.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I could imagine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know why they were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I thought they were waiting there for the morning. I was not supposing anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't that seem rather strange that there they were in the middle of the town in buses and trucks, hundreds of them? Didn't that seem a little odd to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it seemed odd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone comment as to what was -- where these folks were to go the following day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I talked to people, but nobody seemed to know where these people were supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone inform you that they were scheduled to be executed, taken to some place in order to be executed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody made such comments and I had no such thoughts either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Because I had heard what General Mladic had told them. The thought of execution did not cross my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the time while you were there, at that time of the night, did you hear any shooting going on, any firearms being -- going off?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very seldom. One shot, then silence, then another shot. Single shots few and far between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why those shots were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or did you see anyone being abused while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I stayed there very briefly. I talked a little to my colleagues. I was very tired indeed. I went home to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Until the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said earlier -- in your earlier answer you said that you "stayed there very briefly," there meaning where the buses were, where the people were. Do you recall how long, how many hours, you were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you spoke with your colleagues. Who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could not remember now whom I found there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were members of the Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were several of them just when you come into that street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any -- whether there was anyone else there providing security or guarding these buses?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There were some soldiers. I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly who they were, but by their uniforms I could tell that they were not -- their uniforms were dark. It was night and I couldn't notice anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall about what time this would have been, that period of time that you were there, the 15 or 20 minutes or so before you went to your house?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: An hour before midnight or maybe an hour after midnight, in that range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you went to your house. Could you please tell us how long did you stay at your house?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: All night, until the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there and before going to your house, did anyone, any of your colleagues, inform you that you had been requested or that you were needed to remain there for the entire night?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next morning do you recall about what time you left your house?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Between 6.00 and 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Back to town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you go to the -- to have breakfast at the headquarters restaurant, as you had on the morning of the 12th and the 13th, the previous two days?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I'm not sure about where I went first. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you recall where exactly in town you went?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Later, when I arrived, I was about a hundred, maybe 150 metres away from the school. The buses and trucks were no longer there; they had already left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: An hour, two, three. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for staying there for that period of time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I learned from my colleagues that we were assigned to be there to prevent any incidents and to enable the buses to pass smoothly from the school and turn on to the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got there, were all the buses and all the trucks gone?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: From that street, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were there other buses or other trucks on any other streets at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time go inside the school?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. We had no access to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we had no access," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody gave us orders to go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you go around the school at all to canvass the area, to check and see if anything unusual had happened at or near the school?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was not moving around at that time. We had our men standing to the west of the school, but they were ten -- sorry, 100 to 200 metres away from the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever learn whether any Muslim men had been killed in or around the school, either that evening or perhaps even the previous evening? And I'm speaking of the evening of the 13th or maybe even as early as the evening of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I found out that some people had been killed, but I didn't learn anything about when they were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time it would have been when you found out that some people had been killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later, after all that had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did anyone inform you as to who it was that had committed these killings?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Branjevo Farm or Pilica at any point in time during these days?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. To this day, I don't know where the Branjevo Farm is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to participate in any executions in Pilica, for instance?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of your colleagues - and I'm speaking of the Bratunac Brigade military police - whether any of them were in Branjevo Farm or Pilica, be it for killing or securing prisoners to be killed or for any other reasons?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. Nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we know for a fact, we've heard testimony in this courtroom and it's rather substantiated, that sometime in the afternoon or evening of July 13th, 1995, an incident occurred at the Kravica agricultural warehouse. You've already told us that when you went by that evening of the 13th, you did not notice anything. My question is: Did you ever learn of anything happening at that particular location, on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when it was that you learned of this incident.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Later, later. I don't know how much later, but we learnt about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall learning who it was that was responsible for the atrocities that occurred at the agricultural warehouse?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There was one version of the story that a soldier, policeman, or whoever he was had gotten killed there close by, whether inside or right next to it, and anyway, that there was a reaction. And then the guards simply went and killed all the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever hear whether it was members of the Bratunac Brigade that were involved in those executions?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us about witnessing large numbers of individuals in buses and trucks on the evening of the 13th. Could you please tell us whether you have learned what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did learn about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And may I ask: What was it that you learned?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: That all of them had been killed, executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to fastforward a little bit some weeks, months after this period. Do you recall whether you were involved, in any fashion, in what we now know was a reburial process going on in and around that area?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We, policemen, on one or two evenings were in town and we were ordered to watch over the traffic. We were not told anything specific, but when the trucks come that we look after the traffic, avoid anything happening, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall who it was that passed this order on to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you indicated that you weren't told exactly the purpose. Did there come a time when you learned or you figured out what exactly was going on while you were securing that stretch of road or intersection, wherever you were stationed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We realised what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you realised it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: By the very unpleasant smell. There was a strong, unpleasant stench as soon as the trucks arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries to determine who was in charge of this activity?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. It was not our duty to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions. I appreciate your frankness and your honesty. And if you could be as frank and honest with Mr. Stojanovic in the event he may have some questions, the Prosecutors, and the Judges. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further direct questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, sir. We have no questions, Your Honours, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We are almost at the time of the break. Should we take the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if we could perhaps take the break first and I could start after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. We'll take the break and we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I just want to start off where the examination-in-chief ended, when you were in Bratunac. Now, as I understand it, you referred to a school in Bratunac. You indicated that on the 14th of July you were ordered to go to that school. What school were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't an order, let me point out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Going from my home on the 14th, I reached the area in front of the school. I didn't go into the school. I was about 100, 150 metres away from the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what school was that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was known as the Vuk Karadzic school before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you just said to me that it wasn't an order for you to go to the school. I thought you said in your examination-in-chief that you were ordered to go there. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the evening, on the 13th when I arrived from Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to the 14th, sir. You were ordered to go to the Vuk Karadzic school on that day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you ordered to go on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the morning you were ordered to go where?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It was not an order. I found my colleagues there, 100, 150 metres away from the school. And I joined them, because I had been informed that our post for the day was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you went to the Vuk Karadzic school on the 13th, did you see prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on trucks and buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see the prisoners go in the direction of the stadium at -- in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there vehicles parked near the stadium with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever become aware that there were prisoners detained at the soccer stadium on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I learned that there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn there were some prisoners at the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Later. I don't know how many days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "later," from whom did you learn that there were prisoners at the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My colleagues were talking amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're talking about your colleagues, you're referring to other military police from the Bratunac Brigade, is that right? You have to answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you just told us you learned from them there were prisoners detained at the soccer stadium. Can you tell us what they told you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: That there had been prisoners at the stadium and that they were evacuated from there at the same time, on the same day, as the other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would have been the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Don't try to pin me down on dates. When I returned from Han Pijesak, it was night. And they were evacuated the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I just want to move on to an exhibit, and that would be Exhibit P449 for the record, Your Honour. That's the Bratunac Brigade military police daily log. And I would ask the witness to be shown, please, page 15. In the English translation, the date is 15 July 1995. And if we could perhaps put the English translation on the ELMO. Thank you very much, Madam Usher. Now, you see that log there in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that says, it's one sentence, I'll read it slowly. "The police worked on searching and combing the area, as well as apprehending the Muslims found hiding in the area." And below that there are some names. And number 2 it says your name. Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I would like to point out that the Prosecutor is being unfair to the witness. It says "reception," which has nothing to do with the previous paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecution just asked a simple question whether there is his name there and the witness answered that. I think there must be some follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I agree. But to go from they were combing the terrain and seeing his name, and omitting the very critical aspect "reception," which may cue us in to where he was versus what this activity denotes. You know, I just find it strange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think in cross-examination there will be something very strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But after hearing the answers and the questions, you still have the opportunity to clear this up in your re-direct. We'll see what's the question. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So, sir, you're noted down as being at the reception on 15 July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the reception desk at the entrance to the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were -- were you aware then that there were military police combing and searching the area and potentially apprehending Muslims that were found there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that I was aware of that, but I was busy all day at the reception desk. That was my timetable for that night and day. You worked for two hours, then you had two hours of rest, and then went back to work for another two hours, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if Muslims had been captured in the area, they would have been brought to the MP headquarters. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember if any were apprehended. I don't know what they would have done with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the question is, though: If someone had been apprehended, isn't that a logical place to bring prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The reception desk is in a different building. It is not in the same place as the military police headquarters. And if any had been apprehended, they would not have been taken to the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We can then go to 17 July 1995, and I can ask you about that. All right. Now, that is a daily combat -- sorry, that is a daily report dated 17 July 1995. And that says: "The patrol worked at the checkpoints. Air raid sirens sounded at 4.00 a.m. Patrols worked on apprehension and securing of Muslims in municipal area of Bratunac and Srebrenica. One police patrol remained in Pilica to secure and guard the Muslims. All else went according to the plan of the military police command." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I had not seen this before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't aware of the patrol in the area, the police patrol?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one. That's at page 18 in the English translation. There's no date on top, but I believe it should be number 00663910 in the B/C/S version. All right. Now, that report, sir, comes after 18 July and before 20th July, and that states: "During the shift, the police was engaged in notifying conscripts of their deployment. No incidents. Patrols went to secure the public utility workers in Glogova." And underneath "deputy duty officers," number 5 is your name. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were aware of patrols going to secure the public utility workers in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. I was on duty from 4.00 to 5.00 p.m. [as interpreted], according to this. I slept. I was getting some rest on that night, and I was on duty from 4.00 to 5.00, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the mass graves are in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware that there were mass graves that were dug in Glogova with bodies of Muslims placed in those graves?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I knew that they had been dug, but I didn't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to get back to Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm finished with those exhibits, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The transcript notes 4.00 to 5.00 p.m., and I noted that on the exhibit it noted "a.m." It's on page 63, and that would be line 3, lines 2 and 3. Perhaps we could have a clarification before we go on to the next area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we'll go with whatever the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you tell us what time you accompanied General Mladic to Sandici.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The last day of the departure of transports from Potocari, it was the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm asking you about the time of day, though. Can you tell us what time of day it was when you arrived at Sandici and Mladic made his speech.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon. I don't know at what time. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximation in the afternoon. When you say "the afternoon," can you tell us approximately what time you think it was.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: 4.00, 5.00, maybe 6.00. Don't ask me to tell you precisely. It was towards dusk, late afternoon. It could have been even 6.00, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was late afternoon towards dusk. All right. Now, when you said that you saw General Mladic speaking to the prisoners, did you see --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you see anybody call the prisoners balijas?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Mladic was speaking to the prisoners, didn't he also tell the Muslims that if they had surrendered earlier, then there wouldn't have been so many wounded?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything along those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't he also tell the Muslims that they would be taken to Bratunac and that they would get no dinner?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in Sandici boys that were born before 1980 were separated from the rest of the crowd. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, they were all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that some boys tried to get separated and weren't allowed and were told to go back, to sit with the rest of the men?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that, but I wouldn't say that there were any boys there. As far as I can remember and according to my judgement, they were grown-ups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies in the meadow or near the meadow?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In the meadow there, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the meadow?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay much attention. I don't remember seeing anything, just that wounded man who was brought there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. There were hundreds of men that were sitting in the Sandici meadow, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm unable to give you a number, because whatever I may say I'm not sure about it. I can't remember. Whatever I might say may not be correct, so I'd rather not make any attempts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were so many that it would be difficult for you to estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's way above -- I mean, we're taking some leaps here. That's not what the gentleman said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That was another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not what the gentleman said. It's not even another question. It makes an assumption based on the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, maybe you could rephrase your question. Of course, the witness did not know how many prisoners were there. But approximately, there must be a number, hundreds, thousands, or maybe 50. We just need a rough idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say, sir, that there were 100 prisoners there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It is very difficult for me at this point in time to tell you. I didn't have a chance to make an estimate as to the number of people there. I was focusing my attention on other matters. I didn't even make any attempt at estimating the number of people in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Was there so many people there that it would be difficult for you now to make that estimate?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. There weren't that many people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why is it so difficult for you to make the estimate?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just not sure of being able to give you anything close to the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on then to when you went to Nova Kasaba. You saw the men gathered there, right, the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: In Nova Kasaba, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time did you arrive at Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, after that it was, I don't know, maybe an hour, an hour and a half after this, less than an hour. I really don't know. I can't remember the amount of time it takes to get to Kasaba from Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand you correctly, you're approximating about an hour, an hour and a half after Sandici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. About an hour, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us earlier that you spent approximately 30 to 40 minutes in Sandici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to the Nova Kasaba stadium or football pitch, was it not filled with men?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Not quite full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But almost?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many men were there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure, but maybe half of the grass pitch was occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware, sir, that those men had been captured in the woods and brought to Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know, but I noticed some coming of their own accord to the stadium. While I was there, I actually saw them coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there were soldiers there, weren't there, Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when General Mladic spoke to the prisoners at Nova Kasaba, didn't he also tell the Muslim men -- didn't he insult them and curse at them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. He spoke to them quite correctly, politely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't he also tell them that the authorities in Tuzla didn't want them?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He didn't talk about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't there a prisoner, sir, who got up in Nova Kasaba and approached a Serb soldier and the soldier kicked the prisoner and beat him with -- and the soldiers beat him with their rifle butts, and then one of the soldiers shot him?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I did not witness that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, I believe earlier in your examination-in-chief when you were asked about July 12th and what General Mladic had ordered you, you said - and I'm quoting you - "I suppose my superiors knew about the duties given me by Mladic. And nobody asked me anything; I just did the job."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: That was another day. That wasn't the 12th, the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were being asked about the 12th at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correction. The gentleman is correct. It's the 13th, and it was in response to him going back to re-take up his position on the 13th. The record is very clear on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not after that cross-examination, Your Honour. No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't -- that was a deliberate smear towards the cross-examination, and I just would ask again -- I would implore the Court to try to do something about this because it's getting worse and worse and worse. And it's becoming almost impossible to do our job under this daily barrage of this kind of childish behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't said anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait, Mr. Karnavas. From the transcript, I see nothing wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas said: "Not after the cross-examination." Maybe the demeanor, the tone --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't want to waste any time because I have another witness waiting, Your Honour. What I meant was: There was nothing for me to do direct examination based on the cross. Normally re-direct has to clear up something on the cross. There was nothing to clear up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, and I know you're dealing with two Americans here, and I will try to not go into it any further. It was intimately clear what he meant by that to me and to my North American colleague and to any American in the room, absolutely clear. It was a demeaning comment, and to suggest otherwise is absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you have to pardon me from the other jurisdiction, I could not see the difference. But after this sitting, I'll look into the transcript, compare it with the last one Mr. Karnavas made on the same occasion. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I have a question to ask you. I think you testified on the 12th of July General Mladic asked you and a colleague to guard a junction in the Bratunac Brigade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Not to guard it but to watch over the transport, so as to avoid any incidents as the transport passed through that junction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that located in the in Bratunac town, I mean the junction?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I've got a map here. Can you point to me where it is.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you take a pen and draw a circle there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I was advised that this map was used by another witness before, and can you tell me the location of that junction on the map.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Me? Should I point it out? This junction goes from the direction of Potocari, and then there is an intersection of roads. To the left you go to Konjevic Polje; straight ahead you go through town towards Ljubovija; and then to the right there's another street also in town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's not far from the Hotel Fontana, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Very close by. Very close to the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Further examination by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out where the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade are, just so we know.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade was when you pass the intersection and go towards Konjevic Polje, this is not very clear, it is to the left about 150 or 200 metres from the intersection. Somewhere here, on the left-hand side. I'm afraid I can't really find my way. The headquarters was in the former tile factory, ceramic tile factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just one last question. From the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, what was the distance where you were standing at that intersection on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately between 200 and 300 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the Hotel Fontana, how close were you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE JAKOVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It depends if we were at the intersection itself, 70 to 80 metres. Now, if we had something to do to remove the civilians from the roads, from the streets, so we would move around 200, 300 metres, in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room and we wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I wonder if I may be excused. This is Mr. McCloskey's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we sill have some time during this period. Mr. McCloskey, I think the other day you said you filed a kind of correction to your motion on the amendments of the indictment. Is it -- did you file that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We were able to get it to Ms. Stewart last night, and she's written today on that list. So I know she's been getting it all ready to go, and I think it's just a matter of getting her some time to get down to the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, of course you told us that you are going to file your reply today. I don't know where is it? Still in the office?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's -- well, as I noted yesterday, Your Honour, there was a caveat that I would not guarantee that it would be in by 9.00 but that it would be in by 4.30. I anticipate that it will be in sometime around 3.30, 4.00. It is about 95 per cent finished. It's not a superb motion, but I think it does cover the points, in light of the time constraints we have in the middle of the case. We will file it by 3.30 or so this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the other day you applied for the issue of subpoena -- in open court. I would like to know whether you want this subpoena in public or in confidential form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With whom did I -- well, with respect to which witness, Your Honour, if I could be reminded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's go to closed session, please.
